messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The answer depends on what you mean by “planet” and whether you’re looking at our Solar System or the entire observable universe.

| Context | Largest known object |
|---------|---------------------|
| **Within the Solar System** | **Jupiter** – about 11 times the radius of Earth and roughly 318 times its mass. |
| **In the observable universe (confirmed exoplanets)** | **HD 100546 b** – a protoplanet still forming around the young star HD 100546. It has a radius of roughly 2.5 × the radius of Jupiter (≈ 2.5 R_J) and a mass of about 10–20 M_J. It’s the largest *confirmed* planet‑mass object we’ve measured so far. |

> **Why HD 100546 b?**  
>  It was discovered using high‑contrast imaging and is still accreting material from its surrounding disk. Because it’s a protoplanet, its size is still growing, but it already exceeds all other known exoplanets in radius and mass.

> **What about “super‑Jupiters” or “brown dwarfs”?**  
>  Some objects have masses above the deuterium‑burning limit (~13 M_J) and are classified as brown dwarfs rather than planets. The largest *planet‑mass* objects we’ve found are still below this threshold, with HD 100546 b being the biggest.

So, if you’re asking about the largest planet‑mass object we know of, it’s HD 100546 b. If you’re talking about the largest planet in our own Solar System, that’s Jupiter.
